name: Scenario-Based Question

tier.label: Apply — Using Information in New Contexts

summary: Read a short passage or watch content, then answer embedded comprehension questions. Tests understanding of presented material.

aiGenerability.notes: AI generates both passage and comprehension questions. Core Grej-style format. Highly suitable for procedural explanation, narrative comprehension, cause-and-effect reasoning.

passage.description: Prose passage (50–150 words) introducing context, process, narrative, or scenario. Can include quoted dialogue or procedural steps.

questions.description: Array of comprehension questions embedded after or within the passage.

question.description: Comprehension question testing understanding of the passage (inference, recall, cause-and-effect, vocabulary).

options.description: Multiple choice options (2–4 options, depending on age group).

correctIndex.description: Index (0-based) of the correct option in the options array.

explanation.description: Explanation of why the correct answer is right, with reference to the passage.

distractorNotes.description: Brief notes on why each distractor is plausible but incorrect (optional, for teacher reference).

context.description: Optional context label (e.g., 'science: water cycle', 'history: American Revolution', 'language: Spanish conversation'). Helps with content categorization.

ux.mobileNotes: Passage displays in scrollable container. Questions appear one at a time after passage or interspersed. Answer options are large, tappable buttons. Questions fade in with staggered timing (200ms apart) for visual clarity.

ageAdaptations.8-10: Short passage (50 words). 1–2 simple comprehension questions (literal recall, obvious inference). 2 answer options per question. No complex vocabulary. Explanation uses simple language.
ageAdaptations.11-13: Passage (100 words). 2–3 questions (recall, inference, cause-and-effect). 3 answer options per question. Standard vocabulary with occasional context clues. Explanation references specific phrases from passage.
ageAdaptations.14-16: Longer passage (150 words). 3–4 questions (inference, analysis, vocabulary in context, implicit meaning). 3–4 answer options per question. Advanced vocabulary and complex syntax. Explanation may draw connections to broader concepts.
